newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber closes down on thin demand.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber closes down on thin demand.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed lower on continued absence of demand and heavy regional competition, traders said.

Sunny weather since the start of the year has flooded the market with latex and other rubber materials and traders said stiff sales competition was being posed by other rubber producing centres in the region with similar problems.

"There has been no change in the trend since morning," said a trader, adding that it was virtually impossible to lower Malaysian prices to the level of Indonesia or Thailand, as local production costs were much higher.
At the close, February RSS1 buyer was quoted at 301 cents ($1.21) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, down one cent from Friday. February SMR 20 also fell a cent to 296.
Traders offered the SMR 20 at 296 cents a kg, SMR CV at 359, SMR L at 339, SMR 10 at 297 and drum latex FOB at 235.
The INRO five-day average was at 233.77 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Jan 24 from 234.36 on Jan 23. The daily indicator was at 232.09 against 232.91 previously.
